items.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009
items.q: I sat in and played with Albert Ayler the night that I came there, right away.

ctx.x: And how were you thinking? He said they were thinking like you were.

Yeah well he was thinking about trying to play something other than four-four times. Trying to stretch the beat out. Trying to play a little more open and a little more freer. Because that’s what they were doing, and that’s why I felt like I could sit in and play with them. And he just said like there’s people, and he was right, because as soon as I moved to New York, the first night that I got there, Sunny Murray, which is a friend of mine also from Philly who plays drums and he was working with Albert Ayler at…
